doc.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020

chapter: Writing about jazz and reviewing records
title: Making a living as a jazz writer versus a musician
summary: Alkyer says his DownBeat job since 1989 has been steady, but freelance jazz writing is as hard as or harder than being a musician.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: I’m going to start out with an easy one. Which is more challenging, making a living as a jazz musician or making a living writing about jazz musicians?

I will speak of other peoples’ experiences because mine has been pretty good. I, you know, I grew up as a journalist, and my first job in jazz was as the editorial director for DownBeat magazine. I started there in 1989. So for me it’s been a steady paycheck, good work, good work atmosphere, terrific. If you are a freelance jazz writer — very difficult, very difficult. As difficult or more difficult to make a living than it is as a jazz artist/jazz musician. Yeah.
